2Integrals of vector functions

The definite integral of a vector function is defined by the same Riemann sum as in Calc I, and it comes out component by component.

Let .

Definition

Divide into subintervals, each of length . Let be a number in the th subinterval.

Continuing from the definition:

Correction on the board: in the first photo the sum is being written with “” underneath and “” on top. In the finished board it is to , which is what is typed here.

Explanation (added)

Each term is a vector, so the sum can be collected into an part, a part and a part. Each part is an ordinary Riemann sum, and its limit is an ordinary definite integral. So to integrate a vector function you integrate each component separately, and the answer is a vector. (Stewart §13.2, Integrals.)

10Curvature

From here on the board is in blue marker. Curvature measures how quickly a curve changes direction.

Curvature.

is smooth if is continuous.

Definition

The curvature of a curve is

( is “kappa”.) It is the rate of change of the unit tangent with respect to arc length .

Explanation (added)

always has length 1, so the only way it can change is by turning. is how fast it turns. The derivative is taken with respect to and not so that the answer depends only on the shape of the curve and not on how fast you happen to travel along it.

Stewart's definition of smooth has one more condition than the board line: is continuous and . The second part is what makes defined everywhere. (Stewart §13.3, Curvature.)

  • Integrate a vector function. “Evaluate ” or “find given and ”. Integrate each component; an indefinite integral ends with .
  • Find the length of a curve for . Compute , simplify (the examples are chosen so it simplifies), integrate.
  • Reparametrize with respect to arc length measured from a given point in the direction of increasing . Find , solve for , substitute.
  • Find the unit tangent , in general or at a given value of .
  • Find the curvature of a space curve, in general or at a given point, using . Given a point, first find the that produces it.
  • Find the curvature of a graph at a point, and say what happens to as .
